footer.description: One fast game that turns startup theory into decisions you can feel. Built for university startup weeks, pitch nights and founder mixers.
footer.disclaimer: Educational simulation. Multipliers are real 2015–2020 price changes, simplified for gameplay, and not financial advice.

hero.body: A $10,000 portfolio. Five real companies from 2015. One five-year window you cannot see yet. Allocate, lock it in, and wait for the room to reveal what history did.
hero.social: Built for founders, aspiring investors, and the merely curious. No finance degree required.

showcase.revealBody: The host shares one unlock code. Until then, every portfolio stays sealed.

games.title: Play the room.
games.body: One game, two roles. Players allocate in minutes; hosts get a room code, a secret unlock code, and a leaderboard that refreshes without WebSockets.
games.investBody: Start with $10,000. Back five real companies from 2015 before you know how they ended. Lock the portfolio and unlock the 2020 results with the host code.
games.hostBody: Create a room, share the code, and watch every portfolio land on one leaderboard. Manual refresh and light polling keep the screen current.

steps.title: Join the room
steps.body: Enter the room code and a name the leaderboard can recognise. No account, no install.

steps.title: Allocate $10,000
steps.body: Five 2015 companies, five decisions. Spread the budget, concentrate it, or keep some in cash.

steps.title: Unlock together
steps.body: Your portfolio is saved instantly. The host reveals one code when the room is ready.

why.title: Startup theory is tidy.
why.body: The game is built around the messy part: choosing under uncertainty, then discovering what your choices reveal.

lessons.title: Risk only feels real when it is yours
lessons.body: Allocating someone else's money is easy. Watching a $2,500 cheque become zero teaches more than a lecture slide ever will.

lessons.title: The best story does not always win
lessons.body: The first mover does not always win. A beloved product is not a moat if the next platform can do the job. History rewards durable advantages, not headlines.

lessons.title: One room, one reveal
lessons.body: The host controls the reveal. Players cannot unlock their breakdown until the shared code matches on the server.

cta.body: The best way to understand risk is to make a decision and see what happens next. We made that loop fit inside a coffee break.
cta.footnote: No sign-up · no real money · all the lessons
